title: The rules of hooks, and the bugs that breaking them produces

videos.script:
Hooks come with two rules. Call them at the top level of a component, every time. And call them only from components, or from other hooks.

{{order}} The rules look arbitrary until you see what React does with a hook. It does not know your state's names. It knows the order of the calls, and nothing else.

{{crash}} So you will break the first rule, in the way it is usually broken: a return above a hook. The app will not appear at all, and the console will show you the order React expected.

{{quiet}} Then the same mistake in a smaller component. This time nothing crashes. A choice the user made is quietly thrown away, which is worse.

{{lint}} The linter catches both, before anything runs.

{{stale}} And last, a bug that breaks no rule at all. A timer that keeps reading last week, because it was made last week.
